chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard my father (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the owner of the net strikes with the net, whatever is caught in it, whether living or dead, is permissible, except that which does not have a shell/scales, and the floating one of the fish is not to be eaten.'
ai.seo_question: What types of fish are considered halal or haram according to this hadith from al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the method of capture via netting renders the catch permissible whether alive or dead, provided it is not a scaleless variety or floating fish, a distinction often interpreted by Shia jurists as relating to freshness or specific species like catfish. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the intrinsic permissibility of aquatic life unless explicitly prohibited by textual evidence or signs of spoilage, differing slightly from some Sunni schools regarding scaleless fish. The hadith serves as a foundational text for fiqh al-ma'khl (aquatic jurisprudence), highlighting the practical criteria for halal consumption in daily life.
